statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 16 of 100 in the low band, nine points below the 25-point block threshold, because CME equity index futures remain inside the regular weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday and no Nasdaq-100 price path exists to be pathological. Eight of the twenty-four forward slots sit inside that closure. Stress is 69 in the high band. Over the weekend an Iranian cargo vessel was struck near Qeshm Island with one crew member killed and four injured, UKMTO reported a second vessel hit by an unknown projectile, and Russian drones struck a Kyiv-Warsaw passenger train two kilometres from the Polish border along with a fuel station near the Dorohusk-Jagodzin crossing. Poland activated defence and reconnaissance systems while confirming no violation of Polish airspace and no Article 4 consultation. Crude above $100, a 10-year near 4.95 per cent and a Federal Reserve decision on Wednesday complete the backdrop. The single structural checkpoint inside the horizon is the scheduled 22:00 UTC futures restart, published as a narrow danger window running to 03:00 UTC on Monday rather than a broad session-wide state change.
recommendation: Tail sits in the low band, so the deterministic repository mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and this single shared reading applies jointly to NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Three observations support it. First, no venue quotes the Nasdaq-100 in eight of the twenty-four published forward slots: CME equity index futures closed at 21:00 UTC on Friday and are scheduled to resume at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, so there is no gap, no failed retracement and no session extreme available to score. Second, the weekend record has broadened on both vectors, but it is carried in Stress rather than Tail, because Tail measures a pathological price path and no path currently exists to be pathological; the record also remains two-sided, with Monday's Iran-Gulf meeting in Salalah set against the vessel strikes, and with Poland confirming no airspace violation and no Article 4 consultation. Third, the five watch-band slots from 22:00 UTC on Sunday to 02:00 UTC on Monday are published as a narrow evidence-based danger window rather than a broad shutdown, and even the conditional peak Tail of 24 stays one point below the block threshold. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this reading.
headline: CME equity index futures remain inside their scheduled weekend closure with the Nasdaq-100 still at Friday's 29,368.44 close and VIX at 15.84, while two Hormuz vessel strikes and Russian drone strikes on a Kyiv-Warsaw train and a fuel station near the Polish border add unpriced weekend exposure; Tail edges to 16 in the low band because no price path exists to be pathological, and the published risk stays concentrated in the 22:00 UTC restart.
body:
Last observed tape. The Nasdaq-100 closed Friday at 29,368.44, up 0.91 per cent from a 29,103.51 previous close, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 day range, with a 52-week range of 22,841.42 to 30,762.20. The front Nasdaq-100 future settled at 29,387.00, up 0.86 per cent. VIX fell 11.21 per cent to 15.84 from a 17.71 intraday high. That was a relief session inside a week the index finished lower, and it is two-sided, mean-reverting behaviour rather than one-way structure, which is why the published dominant mode is normal.

Cross-asset state. WTI settled at $100.05, down 2.37 per cent on Friday, with Brent at $104.61, down 2.81 per cent, the pullback following Iranian state media confirming that Tehran would meet Gulf states in Oman on the Strait of Hormuz; Brent still finished the week 9.7 per cent higher. H.15 for 10 September shows the 2-year Treasury at 4.56 per cent and the 10-year at 4.95 per cent, both higher across the week, with contemporaneous reporting describing the 10-year as closing in on 5 per cent and the S&P 500 posting its deepest four-day decline since June before Friday's recovery. Crude above $100 alongside a recovering equity tape is a conflict rather than an alignment, and conflicting cross-asset signals raise Stress more than Tail. The shared context file is not used as fresh evidence this hour: its collection timestamp of 12:23 UTC is more than ninety minutes old and its collection status is partial after the calendar section failed, so the macro calendar below and all cross-asset levels rest on independent verification. Its delayed latest-session readings, Nasdaq futures plus 0.86 per cent, VIX futures minus 8.41 per cent, seven of eight megacaps higher and a firm semiconductor complex, are consistent with that independently verified picture but are not treated as live price-path evidence.

Weekend record. Two independent vectors remain unpriced. In the Strait of Hormuz, an Iranian cargo vessel was struck early Sunday off Qeshm Island, killing one of its crew and injuring four, with officials stating that neither the projectile type nor those responsible had been identified; separately, UKMTO reported a further vessel hit by an unknown projectile late Saturday, with a fire brought under control and the crew evacuated. Iran, Gulf Cooperation Council states and Iraq are due to meet in Salalah on Monday on management of the waterway, but a senior Iranian official has said the meeting will not yield a signed agreement, and Bahrain has declined to attend pending restoration of diplomatic ties. That is a genuine two-sided checkpoint with a lowered probability of a resolving outcome rather than a one-way escalation. In Ukraine, Russian drones struck the locomotive of a Kyiv-Warsaw passenger train roughly two kilometres from the Polish border in Volyn region and a fuel station and truck close to the Dorohusk-Jagodzin border crossing, with Ukrainian Railways reporting no injuries on the train because the crew had been warned in advance. Poland activated defence and reconnaissance systems, its interior minister described the events as being treated with the utmost seriousness, and its border guard reported normal traffic at the crossing, no injuries on the Polish side, no violation of Polish airspace and no Article 4 consultation.

Why Tail stays low while Stress is high. Tail measures the probability of a price path that denies meaningful mean reversion for long enough to overwhelm a reverse or grid approach. With the reference contract shut, that path cannot exist, cannot be observed, and cannot be scored. Severe but unpriced headline flow, elevated crude, rising yields and an imminent policy decision are exactly the inputs that belong in Stress, which is why Stress is 69 in the high band while Tail is 16 in the low band. The published forecast caps conditional Tail at 19 for every hour inside the closure for the same reason. Confidence eases one point to 85 to reflect the stale and partial shared context file and the wide venue-to-venue dispersion in reported rate-hike pricing, not any gap in the verified levels.

Horizon and checkpoints. The single structural checkpoint inside the next twenty-four hours is the 22:00 UTC restart of CME equity index futures, published with a conditional peak Tail of 24 and a narrow danger window to 03:00 UTC on Monday. No U.S. macro release falls inside the horizon; the calendar reloads on Tuesday with ADP and the Empire State index, and Retail Sales, the FOMC decision, the Summary of Economic Projections and the Chair's press conference follow on Wednesday at 12:30, 18:00 and 18:30 UTC. Reported rate-hike pricing for that decision moved up over the week after a hot August CPI print, though quoted probabilities differ materially between venues and dates. Those events sit outside this horizon and are recorded in the event calendar rather than in the hourly path.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 14:00 UTC on 12 September to 13:00 UTC on 13 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The whole window sits inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday, and every slot is green with EA_ON and a normal dominant mode. Tail held at 6 for the first fifteen slots, then stepped to 7 at 05:00 UTC, 8 at 06:00, 9 at 07:00, 10 at 08:00, 11 at 09:00, 12 at 10:00, 13 at 11:00, 14 at 12:00 and 15 at 13:00 on 13 September, tracking elapsed time without price discovery rather than any observed structure. Stress traced a shallow U through Saturday, easing from 53 to 50 by 17:00 UTC before rebuilding to 53 at the futures-session boundary, then climbing steadily overnight from 56 to 68 as the Hormuz and Ukraine vectors accumulated. Confidence stayed in the high band throughout, between 85 and 87, because levels, yields, crude and the calendar were verified continuously even though no live price path existed to observe.
outlookSummary: Eight of the twenty-four forward slots lie inside the CME weekend closure; the reference contract is scheduled to resume at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, this horizon's ninth slot. Conditional Tail opens at 16 in the current slot, the only slot describing observed rather than hypothetical conditions, and drifts to 19 by 20:00 UTC as unpriced weekend exposure accumulates across two independent vectors. It is capped at 19 through the closure because a shut contract cannot show the one-way structure Tail measures. The restart slot carries the horizon's conditional peak at 24, the top of the watch band and one point below the block threshold, and five slots from 22:00 UTC to 02:00 UTC on Monday sit in that watch band, published as a narrow danger window to 03:00 UTC rather than a broad shutdown. From 03:00 UTC the path returns to the low band and decays through Asian and European hours to a horizon low of 14, on the conditional assumption that the weekend record reprices through an orderly two-sided auction. That assumption would be invalidated by a gapped restart that extends after failed retracements or holds near a session extreme. Stress peaks at 73 in the restart slot and eases to 62 by the final slot, staying elevated throughout on the unresolved Hormuz situation. Confidence declines from 85 to 72 across the horizon purely as a function of forecast distance from the last verified evidence. The U.S. cash open at 13:30 UTC on Monday falls in the final slot and is published as a checkpoint; Wednesday's FOMC decision falls outside this horizon.
